```markdown
# ces-revisions — roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: partner's words, 2026-11-06. Background: specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-chatgpt.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-claude.md, specs/ces-revisions-research-gemini.md.
Choices made:
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), uv-managed package `ces_revisions`.
- Python/JAX stack named in specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md, Part C implementation notes.

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | How the size of the one-month revision moves with the number of collection days before first release | A | 1 | Release calendar and monthly vintages: a day or two to assemble; fit time on ~40 years of monthly vintages: measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | How much of the one- and two-month revisions comes from late sample reports, and how much from seasonal-factor revision | A | 2 | Reuses the monthly vintages, but needs both the NSA and the SA vintages; fit time: measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | How the size of the two-month revision moves with the first-closing collection rate | A | 3 | Reuses the monthly vintages and the release calendar; collection-rate series: covered in the data inventory of the background files; fit time: measured by Stage 1 |
| O6 | How revision size moves with CES sample size and sample attrition | B | 1 | Covariates hand-built from archived releases; build time and fit time: measured by Stage 2 |
| O4 | How revision size moves with real BLS appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns | B | 2 | Hand-built from budget justifications: several days |
| O5 | How revision size moves with BLS staffing counts | B | 3 | Hand-built from budget justifications and staffing reports: several days |

Tracks: A — collection interval and revision size (research). Rank 1.
B — budget, staffing and attrition (research). Rank 2. Split from A because A rests on sharp month-to-month calendar variation that public release dates give directly. B's covariates move slowly, trend together and must be hand-built. B's answer does not change A's model.

## Stages

Order: the core stages come first, in the partner's track ranking (A, then B). Stage 2's dependency on Stage 1's vintage data agrees with that order.

- [ ] Stage 1: Collection days and one-month revision size (Track A core)
      Objective: Deliver O1 end to end on real CES vintages, at the smallest standard that gives a usable estimate.
      Outcomes: O1
      Track: A
      Consumes: nothing (the package is a scaffold with smoke tests)
      Produces: real monthly CES vintages and the release calendar, held in the repo's data layer; a first fitted model of one-month revision size; specs/ces-revisions-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: The findings file reports the estimated relationship between collection-day count and one-month revision size, with its uncertainty, from a fit on real vintages over the full available span. The file also records the measured cost of the real run: time to assemble the vintages and the calendar, the data volume, and the wall time of the fit.
      Leaves out: the seasonal-factor versus late-sample split (Ranked list A, item 1); the first-closing rate (Ranked list A, item 2); the benchmark and post-benchmark stages, supersector pooling, structural-change handling, a vintage manifest, and the full validation suite (Ranked list A, item 3)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Sample size, attrition and revision size (Track B core)
      Objective: Deliver O6 end to end on real data, with the hand-built sample-size and attrition series joined to the Stage 1 vintages.
      Outcomes: O6
      Track: B
      Consumes: the Stage 1 monthly vintages and the revision measure (plan <id>, Handoff)
      Produces: hand-built monthly or annual sample-size and attrition series; specs/ces-revisions-stage-2-findings.md
      Exit: The findings file reports the estimated relationship between sample size and attrition and revision size, with its uncertainty, from a fit on real data. The file also records the measured cost: hours to hand-build the series, and the wall time of the fit.
      Leaves out: appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdowns (Ranked list B, item 1); staffing (Ranked list B, item 2); the joint identification of the collinear slow covariates (Ranked list B, item 3)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Ranked list — Track A
1. O3 — needs the NSA and the SA vintages; cost re-estimated from the Stage 1 findings
2. O2 — needs the collection-rate series; cost re-estimated from the Stage 1 findings
3. Later qualities, not yet ranked by the partner: the benchmark and post-benchmark revision stages, supersector pooling, structural-change handling, a vintage manifest, the full validation suite — place at the first resume

## Ranked list — Track B
1. O4 — several days to hand-build from budget justifications
2. O5 — several days to hand-build from budget justifications and staffing reports
3. Later quality, not yet ranked by the partner: the joint identification of the collinear slow covariates — place at the first resume

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, and writing-plans copies it verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

Retire when every outcome O1–O6 is either delivered by a ticked stage or consciously deferred with a written why (derive-roadmap §6, run over the Outcomes list). Each verdict cites its stage, its plan and its findings file. A stopped track parks its Ranked list into specs/deferred_items.md (§5).
```
